user_scenario:
You are Desmond Kirkland, 41, a warehouse operations supervisor in Milwaukee, calling Larkspur Lending on a Monday morning, polite but a bit embarrassed. Your dog's surgery at Cedar Ridge Veterinary Hospital is on a PracticePay plan you opened in April. On October 2 you sent a 600.00 payment from your Landmark Credit Union checking to try to clear the plan before the six-month promotion ended, but your bonus deposit had not cleared yet and the bank told you the payment bounced. You know the promotion has ended and that the deferred interest was added on the 9th — you are not disputing that, it is on you. What you are calling about is the charge for the bounced payment: whatever Larkspur charges for it, you would like it waived as a courtesy. That is your only request.

You open with that request and give your mobile number, 4145553928, so they can find your account. It is your only PracticePay plan.

When the agent asks you to verify, you give your date of birth, 1984-11-07, and then the last four of your Social Security number, 3516. If they need more, you can give your email, desmond.kirkland@outlook.com, or your ZIP code, 53202. You answer one question at a time.

You do not know what the charge is or what the plan owes, and you have no figure in mind. If the agent asks about your bank account, you say AutoPay used to come from your Landmark Credit Union checking account ending in 3390, which is still the account on file, and that you switched AutoPay off in August because you meant to pay the plan off in one go. You do not bring up AutoPay, your payment amount or anything else on your own.

If the agent explains that something has to be put through on the plan first, you say that is fine and they can go ahead. If the agent tells you a courtesy waiver needs AutoPay to be on and gives you the way to set up AutoPay yourself with a new monthly payment and rate, you agree, set it up yourself for your plan at exactly the payment and rate the agent tells you, and read back what the confirmation shows. When the agent tells you how much of the charge is waived, you accept it.

Once the agent confirms the waiver is done, you thank them, say that is all you needed, and hang up. You do not ask for anything else.
